subject: Audit access coordination & rolling evidence plan
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@medtechco.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medtechco.com>, Legal Team <law@medtechco.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify SOC 2 evidence cadence and pen-test access in Order Form

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the draft order form. A couple items the procurement and legal teams asked us to clarify before we route to signature:

- Pen-test access: we need to know the expected notice period for a customer-initiated pen test, whether access is limited to staging, and how credentials/keys are handled during the window.
- SOC 2 / evidence cadence: procurement expects a monthly delivery of sampled logs for the past 30 days and a quarterly full SOC 2 snapshot. Can Redwood confirm what you can commit to and what level of log extracts (fields + retention) you can provide?
- Inspection scope: we prefer an "inspection-lite" approach—sample-based review with a 10-business-day notice and scoped questions rather than full on-site inspections. Will Redwood accept language like that in the security exhibit?

I attached a redline from our side (we'll send the formal redline from Legal separately), but wanted to confirm the operational pieces first.

Appreciate a short reply with the operational plan so we can align legal/ops on our side.

Best,
Emily Zhang
Director, Security & Compliance
MedTechCo

Attachments: MT_Request_Security_Qs.pdf (summary)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@medtechco.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medtechco.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify SOC 2 evidence cadence and pen-test access in Order Form

Emily —

Thanks for the clarity. High level answers and next steps below so your legal/procurement teams have something concrete to review before formal redlines: 

1) Pen-test access and window:
- We support customer-initiated pen tests against a staging environment by default.
- Standard notice: 30 calendar days.
- Access scope: role-based staging accounts with scoped data (no production PHI/PII).
- Credentials/keys: short-lived credentials issued per test; KMS-handled keys remain under Redwood control and will not be exported.

2) SOC 2 / evidence cadence:
- We can provide sampled log extracts monthly (last 30 days) with fields: timestamp, request path, user-id hash, region, auth event, and outcome.
- Full SOC 2 snapshot (attestation report) provided quarterly or upon request subject to a reasonable cadence (we propose quarterly).
- Retention: live logs retained for 90 days in staging extracts; we can agree to provide an archived extract on request (see retention section for longer-term retention as an add-on).

3) Inspection scope:
- We can accept an "inspection-lite" clause: sample-based evidence requests, 10 business days' notice, and mutually agreed sampling criteria. For more invasive inspections (privileged access or on-site), we'd require a separate scoped agreement.

Next steps: I'm looping in our Security and Legal leads to draft a short exhibit you can attach to the Order Form. I attached our initial redline of the Order Form (format only). If the high-level items above look OK, I'll share proposed exhibit language.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: MT_OrderForm_Redline_v1.pdf (redline stub)

Also flag any exposure in our standard MSA/order form if we accept monthly sampled extracts.

Logan / Karthik / Emily —

Thanks for the primer. Below are practical ops/legal-friendly bullets I recommend we include in the exhibit. I've kept them short so Legal can fold them into the Order Form:

- Pen-test window:
  - Customer may request a pen-test against Redwood-managed staging with 30 calendar days' notice.
  - Redwood will provision scoped, short-lived IAM credentials for the test; credentials will expire at end of window.
  - No production data (PHI/PCI) will be exposed in staging; any synthetic or masked data will be used.
  - Redwood on-call contact provided for the test window (phone + pager) to triage findings.

- Evidence cadence / logs:
  - Monthly sampled extracts: last 30 days; fields delivered as CSV or S3 export: timestamp, request_id, api_path, operation, actor_hash, auth_result, latency_ms, error_code.
  - Standard extract retention: 90 days. Customers may request archived extracts (12 months) as an add-on; add-on terms addressed in Order Form appendix.
  - Quarterly SOC 2 snapshot: delivery of the attestation report and complementary control narrative.

- Inspection-lite clause (proposed legal language):
  - "Customer may, upon 10 business days' written notice, request sample-based evidence related to controls in the Security Exhibit. Redwood will fulfill requests by producing sampled logs and attestation materials. Requests requiring privileged access, live production inspection, or extended forensic analysis shall be subject to a separate scoped SOW and additional fees."

- Security controls / key management:
  - Redwood will retain control of KMS keys; customers will receive signed attestations and key-rotation reports but keys will not be exported.
  - Vulnerability/pen-test findings will be triaged via the agreed JIRA process; critical findings will be escalated to execs within 48 hours.

Attachments: pen-test-checklist.xlsx (ops checklist stub), proposed-security-exhibit-diff.txt (wording draft).

If this looks good to you all, Karthik can tighten the legal phrasing and I can produce a final ops appendix we can attach.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Security & Trust | Redwood Inference

If Redwood confirms that an archived 12-month export can be produced on request (with pricing / lead time to be added to the Order Form appendix), we will instruct Legal to send a formal redline and circulate to your team for sign-off.
